data.why: The repo ships no example PDFs (papers/ only has a .gitkeep and README), so a hand-built PDF with text content designed to trip GRIM, statcheck, p-hacking, sample-size, Western-blot-loading-control, blacklist-wording and title/conclusion-gap checks stands in for an uploaded manuscript, plus a CSV with a narrow-range numeric column, a missing cell, an out-of-range duplicate value, and a cross-column high-precision duplicate for the Benford/identical-values checks.

goals: Upload a candidate paper PDF and run the full forensic pipeline to get an overall risk score and red/orange/yellow signal breakdown
Drill into a specific flagged signal (e.g. GRIM inconsistency or a p-hacking cluster) and read the evidence and human-review instructions behind it
Attach a supplementary data table (CSV) alongside the PDF to extend numeric checks (Benford's law, duplicate-value detection) beyond what's reported in the text
Run Western blot / image forensic checks (LUT false-color, ELA, clone detection) and judge from the generated comparison images whether a figure looks manipulated
Export a Markdown/JSON summary of the review suitable for sharing with a co-reviewer

review.summary: I'd file it after fixes. The text and statistical side is captured accurately, with good evidence: upload, run, severity dashboard, per-signal evidence cards, export. The image-forensics and side-by-side comparison workbench and the LLM, PubPeer and Q&A layer, which the README presents as the core of the tool, are missing or empty, so the tree needs a re-run with images and some cleanup of test-only nodes.
